claims.text: Nickel-based superalloy components will have improved erosion resistance in liquid aluminum at 700°C.
The proposed nickel-based superalloy is initially in the solid state.
The proposed intervention is immersion in liquid aluminum at 700°C for 100 hours.
A protective aluminum oxide layer will form on the nickel-based superalloy surface during immersion.
Literature verifies protective aluminum oxide formation on nickel-based superalloys under high-temperature liquid-aluminum conditions.
The aluminum-resistant alloying principle of nickel-based superalloys enables formation of a stable protective oxide layer.
The stable protective oxide layer reduces corrosion and erosion by liquid aluminum.
The nickel-based superalloy will reduce erosion rate by 30% relative to currently used materials.
The predicted 30% erosion-rate reduction is based on empirical evidence from similar alloy systems.
Currently used materials have an average mass loss of 1.2 g/cm² over 100 hours.
The desired erosion rate is below 0.5 g/cm² per 100 hours.
Performance may vary with the specific nickel-based superalloy composition.
Performance may vary with the exact conditions of the liquid-aluminum environment.
The hypothesis is falsified if mass loss exceeds 0.6 g/cm² over 100 hours.

contradictions.description: A 30% reduction from the stated baseline of 1.2 g/cm² gives 0.84 g/cm² over 100 hours. This exceeds both the desired boundary of 0.5 g/cm² and the falsification threshold of 0.6 g/cm², so the numerical predicted outcome would itself falsify the hypothesis.
